references.note: Approved ground-critter disc, camera, upper-left lighting and finish; copy only the disc/camera/lighting/finish, not the rat body plan.

Native identity, inspected at 8x scale: massive curved mandibles that are visibly PALE ivory-grey where the rest of the head/body is glossy jet-black -- a value-contrast cue inside the creature itself, not just a size cue. Mandibles project forward well past the front legs and are wider than the head. Matches native desc 'a large black ant with huge mandibles' (ant.lua line 63) and the native's faster movement_speed=1.3 (leaner/quicker build).

prompt_fields.subject: One giant carpenter ant seen from a steep overhead three-quarter angle: a compact insect body with a rounded thorax and a large glossy black gaster, six legs splayed in a lightly raised, quick-moving stance. A pair of massive mandibles curve open and project far forward from the head, clearly wider than the head itself and reaching past the front legs -- unmistakably the biggest bite in the family. The mandibles are a distinct pale ivory-grey, several value steps lighter than the glossy jet-black head and body they attach to, exactly like the native reference's pale-tipped huge mandibles. Chitin elsewhere is smooth and glossy black with only a small, tight highlight confined to the crown of the thorax.
prompt_fields.contrast: This is a new six-member family (white, brown, carpenter, blue, yellow, black ant) sharing one body plan; siblings must not be told apart by hue alone, and this identity shares its native black colour with giant black ant, so it needs a second, non-colour cue that survives 48px. Give carpenter ant two independent cues black ant does not have: (1) silhouette -- mandibles wider than the head, curved open, projecting past the front legs, unlike black ant's small mandibles that stay tucked inside the head's own outline; (2) an internal value contrast -- the pale ivory-grey mandibles read as a bright patch against the dark head/body even in grayscale at 48px, unlike black ant's mandibles which are the same near-black tone as its head and produce no internal contrast at all. Do not rely on a broad rim-light or glossy sheen as the distinguishing cue; the mandible shape and the mandible-vs-head value jump are the primary cues, present in both colour and grayscale.
prompt_fields.composition: One complete six-legged ant centred on one circular disc, steep overhead three-quarter view, body angled so the head, mandibles and two or three legs read clearly; the mandibles, every leg and antenna stay inside the disc with the outer sixth of the disc radius left as bare base plate. Keep the head and mandibles out of the upper-right rank corner and upper-left interaction corner. No second creature, no web, no burrow, no scenery. Base-plate discipline, calibrated: this exact style-reference/composition pairing has now been measured four times for this ant family redraw -- two fresh generations averaged +12.2 base_drift (too bright) and two directed edits asking for a full ~12-unit darkening overshot to about -19.5 (too dark by roughly 2.5x the requested amount). Render the neutral disc -- including the whole outer-sixth ring band -- about 8 RGB luminance units darker than the style reference's disc (not identical, and not a full shade darker either): aim for a small, deliberate undershoot on the dark side rather than matching what looks correct at a glance, since this composition's default is measurably too bright. Do not darken the creature itself to compensate -- the creature's own tones stay exactly as specified above; only the disc plate takes this small intentional downward bias. Add no warm cast, glow, bounce-light, gradient or vignette to the disc anywhere, including directly under or behind this black-bodied creature.
prompt_fields.palette: Glossy jet-black chitin over most of the body, with the pair of mandibles rendered a distinctly lighter warm ivory-grey (not white, not glossy chrome -- a matte-to-satin pale horn tone) that reads as a clear bright patch against the black head at every size; a single small, tight, cool-white highlight on the dorsal thorax ridge only, not spread along the body edges; deep black-brown shading in the leg joints and creases; restrained copper-grey neutral bevel and charcoal disc held at the style reference's exact lightness; no colored faction aura.
